title: Aloo Gobi
subtitle: Spiced potato and broccoli
excerpt: Aloo gobi is a dry-style Indian curry that lets a simple spice base do the work. Cauliflower is traditional, but broccoli works just as well and is easier to source year-round. The dish is quick to put together and pairs with dal or a simple raita.
sourceNotes: Aloo gobi is a staple of North Indian home cooking and Punjabi cuisine. The name translates as potato and cauliflower, and the dish appears in countless variations across the subcontinent.

content.text: Keep the heat at medium once the lid goes on. Too high and the potatoes scorch on the outside before they cook through; too low and they become watery.

items.prepNote: cut into small florets (cauliflower is traditional and works equally well)

content.text: Heat the sunflower oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 30 seconds. Add the onion and cook for 7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until golden.
Add the garlic, ginger, turmeric, and coriander-ground. Stir and cook for 2 minutes, then add the diced tomato. Cook for a further 3 minutes until the tomato breaks down.
Add the potato cubes and stir to coat. Season with salt, add 100 ml of water, cover, and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Add the broccoli florets, stir gently, replace the lid, and cook for a further 8 minutes until both the potato and broccoli are tender.
Remove the lid, sprinkle over the garam masala, and stir gently. Taste and adjust seasoning. Scatter the fresh coriander over the top before serving.

items.symptom: The broccoli has gone soft and grey
items.cause: It was added too early or cooked with the lid on for too long
items.fix: Add broccoli in the last 6 to 8 minutes only, and check it frequently. It should retain some bite.

items.symptom: The dish is sticking to the pan
items.cause: Not enough oil, or the heat is too high
items.fix: Add a splash of water and reduce the heat. Stir and scrape the base; the fond adds flavour.
